name: PulseMonitor
summary: Uptime monitoring for developers and small teams: HTTP, API, port, keyword and SSL checks with incident history, plus a built-in SEO site audit; free plan with 50 monitors and a paid plan for 1-minute checks, webhooks, status pages and heartbeats.
best_for: developers and small teams who want HTTP, API, SSL and keyword uptime checks plus a basic SEO audit in one cheap tool, with a free plan that covers 50 monitors
skip_if: you need multi-location checks, phone or SMS alerting, or a vendor whose legal entity and jurisdiction are stated in its terms, or you want the option of a refund on a yearly plan
honest_knock: The refund policy is strict: monthly and yearly fees are non-refundable, including the unused part of a year, so the $90 annual plan is a commitment. Neither the terms nor the refund policy name the company behind PulseMonitor or the country whose law applies; the terms say only the jurisdiction in which we operate. The free plan checks every 5 minutes and alerts only by email, Discord and Telegram, while Slack, PagerDuty, status pages and cron heartbeats need Pro. The SEO analyzer is a one-click site audit, not rank tracking. We have not used PulseMonitor ourselves. The 'Last updated' line on the terms, refund and security pages read 14 October 2026 when we read them on 14 October and 25 October 2026 when we read them on 25 October, so it follows the day of reading and does not tell you when the wording last changed. The terms cap liability at the greater of the fees paid in the previous 12 months or $100, and say PulseMonitor has no obligation to keep your data after termination. PagerDuty alerts need Zapier or your own proxy.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Pro · per account per month, or $90 a year
pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-14 in a live browser on pulsemonitor.io/pricing, the home page and the refund policy dated 14 October 2026) Two plans, no per-seat pricing. Free costs nothing and needs no credit card: 50 monitors at a 5-minute check interval, HTTP, port (TCP) and keyword monitoring, email alerts for down and recovered, Discord and Telegram, an incident timeline with uptime and response-time stats, SSL expiry checks, the one-click SEO analyzer and 3 months of data retention. Pro is $9 a month or $90 a year: 1-minute checks, 500 monitors, ping (ICMP), DNS and JSON/API response monitors, webhook alerts with escalation, teams and roles, unlimited status pages, maintenance windows, unlimited heartbeat monitors for cron jobs and workers, REST API access, SEO audit export and 24 months of retention. The refund policy says fees for monthly and annual subscriptions are non-refundable, with no prorated refund on cancellation; refunds are at the vendor's discretion for billing errors, extended service failure or where the law requires one. Re-read on 25 October 2026 with a plain fetch of pulsemonitor.io/pricing: both plans, their limits and the feature matrix unchanged. The documentation marks the Ping and JSON monitor types and the REST API as Pro-only, and the features page says team monitors do not count against your personal monitor limit.

compare_with.name: UptimeRobot
compare_with.why: UptimeRobot is in our dossiers too: Free at $0 and Solo from $144 a year, quoted yearly, read over a US connection on 26 August 2026 and re-checked in euros on 29 September 2026. PulseMonitor, read on 14 October 2026, is $90 a year on Pro for 500 monitors at 1-minute checks with status pages and heartbeats, and adds an SEO analyzer that UptimeRobot does not sell. UptimeRobot is the older, larger service with more published detail about who runs it; PulseMonitor is cheaper on paper and bundles SEO audits.
